subject: VPC / On-prem feasibility — governance, staffing, exceptions
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC / On-prem feasibility — governance, staffing, exceptions

Team —

I pulled together a short set of asks from last week's customer sync with AtlasHealth. They're asking for a private VPC deployment with optional on-prem appliance (air-gapped) for one business unit. Before we commit product-side, I need cross-functional clarity on governance, resourcing, and any exception lanes we should surface. Key items below — please respond with owners and rough T-shirt estimates by EOD Monday.

1) Governance model: who owns the private control plane (Redwood vs. customer-managed)? What audit trails / role mappings are required for onboarding?
2) Staffing: minimal SRE on-call, integration engineer effort, and expected product PM coverage for a pilot (6–8 weeks).
3) Exceptions: what nonstandard requests trigger legal/infosec escalation (HSM, airgap, custom kernel builds)?
4) Deliverables for proposal: ops matrix, security evidence list (SOC2 partial), and a draft MOA for EdgeOps partner.

Attachments: private-deploy-ops-matrix.xlsx (ops/resourcing table) — please open and annotate.

Notes: Atlas procurement is asking for a high-level runbook and an MOA draft to circulate to their legal team ASAP. I put Beth (Atlas) and EdgeOps on the external thread — they were on the call but I haven't looped them in yet; will do after we get internal alignment.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Lead, Partner Deployments
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: private-deploy-ops-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC / On-prem feasibility — governance, staffing, exceptions

Vanessa — quick notes from an architecture perspective:

- Control plane: we should push for customer-managed VPC with Redwood private control plane (managed tenant) for pilot. That keeps sensitive keys on their side while we retain orchestration.
- Audit trails: we can provide per-request trace IDs and an exportable audit log; will need to confirm retention windows (default 90 days) — legal may want longer.
- Staffing: for a single pilot cluster: 0.5 FTE infra eng during onboarding, 0.2 FTE SRE on-call for steady-state (assuming no bespoke kernel work), plus a product PM quarter effort. Table updated with these numbers.

Open questions which impact estimates:
- Does Atlas require HSM-backed key sealing? If yes, onboarding jumps to 2.0 FTE infra.
- Air-gapped appliance: ops & security require a hardened build and an offline install path (adds 3–4 weeks and a dedicated integration engineer).

I'm adding inline comments to the ops matrix. If we decide on a managed-control-plane approach we should quantify support SLAs (target 99.9 for pilot).

— Karthik
Senior Staff Engineer
[Quoted text]

From: Beth Carter <beth@atlashealth.com>

Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com, EdgeOps Partnerships <partners@edgeops.io>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC / On-prem feasibility — governance, staffing, exceptions

Thanks Vanessa — and thanks Karthik for the quick notes. A few clarifications from our side to help you size: 

- HSM: our security team has a hard preference for HSM for keys that sign patient-related payloads. We can accept an HSM-backed KMS in-cloud as long as the crypto boundary is customer-controlled.
- Retention: we need 365-day audit log retention for the pilot window (we can archive older logs to S3).
- On-prem appliance: the BU in question wants an option to host inference on-prem during the pilot for a small % of traffic (10–15%) for latency-sensitive workflows; timeline is tight — ideally a 6–8 week pilot kickoff from agreement.

We're happy to share our procurement doc with timeline constraints — attaching our scope questions and a high-level procurement checklist. If you can confirm the minimal on-call expectations and a rough delivery timeline (week-by-week), we'll prioritize the legal review.

Best,
Beth Carter
Dir, Product Ops — AtlasHealth
[Attachment: atlas-scope-questions.pdf (pdf)]

Date: Mon, 01 Sep 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC / On-prem feasibility — governance, staffing, exceptions

Thanks everyone — consolidated next steps and owners below. I'm kicking off a short internal decision lane and will share a one-page we can send to Atlas/legal by EOD Wednesday.

Decisions agreed (internal):
- Control plane: default to "Customer-managed VPC + Redwood private control plane (managed tenant)" unless Atlas requests full control-plane handoff. Owner: Karthik.
- HSM: treat as an escalation. If Atlas requires HSM-backed sealing, we route to Security + Legal for a contract exception (estimated +1.5 FTE infra during onboarding). Owner: Priyom.
- Retention: support 365-day audit retention for pilot; Ops will wire an S3 archival flow. Owner: Priyom.
- On-prem appliance: opt-in pilot path (adds ~4 weeks to timeline). Owner: Karthik / EdgeOps for packaging.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Karthik: finalize a week-by-week pilot timeline and SLA table (WIP) — ETA: Tue COB (2028-09-02).
- Priyom: compile security evidence we can share (SOC2 mappings, key management options) and start legal intake for HSM exception — ETA: Wed EOD (2028-09-03).
- Vanessa: draft one-pager for Atlas/legal and circulate to Beth + procurement — ETA: Wed EOD (2028-09-03).
- Stephanie: open JIRA INF-4321 for tracking and add HubSpot note (98345).

Attachments: draft-moa-edgeops.docx (placeholder MOA for partner).

Beth — would you and procurement be comfortable getting the MOA and the one-page timeline? If yes, we'll send both together.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Partner Success, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: draft-moa-edgeops.docx (docx)]
